title: Make heartbeat report presence kinds and demand reattachment
description:
Objective: turn the heartbeat from a bare liveness ping into the channel that tells a runner it must reattach. packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/heartbeat.ts currently acknowledges a ping even when no worker record exists, so a sidecar keeps pinging happily after a restart wiped its worker and nothing tells it to re-register.

Deliverable: heartbeat accepts a presence kind from the sidecar, distinguishing process presence, provider presence, waiting for input and observed progress, and records it on the attempt. When the caller's worker record or attempt is missing, or its attempt is in phase reconciling, the response tells the runner that reattachment is required instead of acknowledging normally.

Not in scope: the wrapper sidecar changes that send the new field and act on the reattach instruction; that is the sibling wrapper task. The tool must stay non-blocking and cheap, since it fires every 60 seconds per seat.

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/heartbeat.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: heartbeat accepts an optional presence kind of process, provider, waiting or progress and records the latest one on the attempt
A heartbeat whose worker record or attempt is missing returns a reattach-required response rather than a plain acknowledgement
A heartbeat against an attempt in phase reconciling also returns reattach-required
An old-style heartbeat with no presence kind still succeeds, so an un-upgraded wrapper keeps working
The tool remains non-blocking and adds no new disk write per ping beyond the attempt presence field
npx vitest run src/tools/heartbeat.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Heartbeat must stay non-blocking; it must never be marked blocking:true.
An older wrapper that sends no presence kind must keep working unchanged.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE SEAM AND CONFIRM ONE CROSS-TASK INTERACTION (read-only, no edits). No acceptance case owns this card, so the card itself is the contract — checked by grepping this task id against src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, which returns nothing. Read packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/heartbeat.ts; it is 34 lines. Today it requires a workerId, calls `state.touchWorker` and returns a bare acknowledgement, and its own comment explains why touchWorker no-ops on a missing or dead record — which is exactly the defect: a sidecar whose worker was wiped keeps getting an acknowledgement forever. Note it does NOT wrap itself in runExclusive, because tool dispatch is already serialized through the global state mutex; do not add one, and keep the handler cheap, since it fires every sixty seconds per seat. Read the ExecutionAttempt interface in src/types/schema.ts and the attempt store's exported functions, in particular `listAttempts`, `currentAttempt` and `setAttemptPhase`. NOW THE INTERACTION THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN: `setAttemptPhase` stamps `lastPhaseAt`, and the reconcile-window sweep planned in task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c measures its window from exactly that field. If a presence ping refreshed `lastPhaseAt`, a reconciling attempt would become immortal and that sweep would silently never fire. So presence must be written by its own dedicated store function that never touches `lastPhaseAt` and never goes through the phase setter. Verify that sweep's measurement field by reading it, and record the finding in the step note. Finally, confirm whether `moe.reattach_attempt` from task-58f7db9a9e44469e9351b2cdea73b47d has landed, since the reattach-required response should point at it by name; if that tool is not registered yet, still name it in the response and say so in the note rather than inventing a different surface. Read docs/MCP_SERVER.md's existing heartbeat section for the format you will extend. Produce no diff in this step.

READ-ONLY. No diff produced.

CONFIRMED, by reading:
1. Reconcile-window sweep measures from `lastPhaseAt`. `src/state/sweeps.ts:218` `const phaseAt = attempt.lastPhaseAt ? Date.parse(attempt.lastPhaseAt) : NaN;` then `:221 if (nowMs - phaseAt <= state.reconcileWindowMs) continue;`. Its header (:195) pins it: "The clock is the attempt's own `lastPhaseAt` — when it ENTERED the phase". `setAttemptPhase` (attemptStore.ts:~225) stamps `lastPhaseAt: new Date().toISOString()` on every real change. So a presence ping routed through the phase setter WOULD make a reconciling attempt immortal and silently disable that sweep. Presence gets its own writer; test asserts stored bytes.
2. `moe.reattach_attempt` HAS landed and is registered — `src/tools/index.ts:27` import, `:118` in getTools(); `src/tools/reattachAttempt.ts` exists with 20 unit cases. The reattach-required response can name it truthfully, not aspirationally.
3. No acceptance case owns this card: `grep -c task-06b658be6e2c4b4bbfaab2f7f200e1f5 src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` = 0 (exit 1). The card is the contract.
4. heartbeat.ts is 34 lines, registered at `src/tools/index.ts:151`, NOT `blocking:true`, NOT wrapped in runExclusive (dispatch already serializes). Keeping both as-is.
5. Attempt resolution path: `currentAttempt(state, taskId)` returns the highest-generation non-closed attempt; OPEN_PHASES = running|finalizing|reconciling. Worker -> `currentTaskId` -> currentAttempt is the ownership path; will also require `attempt.workerId === workerId` so a ping never records presence on a peer's attempt (folded into the no-open-attempt reason, not a fourth condition).
6. ExecutionAttempt (schema.ts:886) already carries optional advisory hints `processStartedAt`/`host` with an explicit "never evidence of liveness" comment — the new presence fields belong in that same spirit and same optionality, so no migration.
7. PRE-EXISTING TEST THAT MUST FLIP: heartbeat.test.ts "is a no-op for an unknown worker (never throws)" asserts `resolves.toEqual({ ok: true })`. Under the new contract a missing worker returns reattach-required, so that case gets repointed in step 2 — it is not a regression.

The 12 that fail on today's code (every one for the right reason — the tool acknowledges unconditionally and no presence field exists):

- records presence kind process|provider|waiting|progress on the caller's open attempt (4 cases, it.each)

The 5 that pass today are the compatibility guards, and they are supposed to pass on both sides: refreshes lastActivityAt for a live worker; does not resurrect a DEAD worker; succeeds unchanged for an old-style ping carrying no presence kind; writes nothing to the attempt file when no presence kind is supplied (byte + mtime compare); leaves lastPhaseAt byte-identical when it records presence (vacuous today, load-bearing after step 3/4 — this is the reconcile-window guard).

CONTRACT THE TESTS PIN (step 3/4 must match it exactly):
- wire param `presenceKind`, optional, one of `process` | `provider` | `waiting` | `progress`
- stored on the attempt as `presenceKind` + `presenceAt` (ISO)
- acknowledgement is exactly `{ ok: true }` for old-style AND presence pings (no shape drift for an un-upgraded wrapper)
- reattach response is RETURNED: `{ ok: false, reattachRequired: true, reason, reattachWith: 'moe.reattach_attempt', attemptId?, phase? }` with stable reasons `no-worker-record` | `no-open-attempt` | `attempt-reconciling`; attemptId/phase present only for the reconciling case
- an unknown presenceKind THROWS a MoeError (invalid input) and stores nothing

DESIGN NOTE FOR QA: an open attempt whose `workerId` is a different seat is folded into `no-open-attempt` rather than a fourth reason — the ping must never record presence on a peer's attempt, and from the caller's side "not yours" and "not there" both mean re-register. implementationPlan.description: DECLARE THE PRESENCE FIELDS AND THEIR OWN WRITER. In packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts add an exported union for the presence kind with exactly the four members the card names — process presence, provider presence, waiting for input, and observed progress — and add two optional fields to ExecutionAttempt: the latest presence kind and the timestamp it was reported. Both optional, so every existing attempt record stays valid with no migration, matching how the store's other optional hints were added. Comment them honestly, in the same spirit as the existing note on the process hints: a reported presence kind is what a sidecar CLAIMS about its own state, not something the daemon verified, so nothing may treat it as proof of liveness — at best it narrows what a human or a later probe should ask about. Then add one exported function to src/state/attemptStore.ts that records presence on an attempt: it takes the attempt id and the kind, writes the two fields through the store's existing persist-then-publish ordering, and MUST NOT touch `lastPhaseAt` or go anywhere near the phase setter, for the reason established in step 1 — the reconcile-window sweep measures from that field and a presence ping must never extend it. Say that in the function's comment so the next person does not 'simplify' it into setAttemptPhase. Refuse an unknown kind as invalid input rather than storing it, and treat a missing attempt as a named error the caller can handle rather than a silent no-op.

`src/types/schema.ts`:
- New exported union `AttemptPresenceKind = 'process' | 'provider' | 'waiting' | 'progress'`, declared right under `ExecutionAttemptPhase`, with a comment giving each member its meaning (process subprocess still there / in a provider call / parked waiting for input / observed the execution move) and the honest boundary in both directions: a kind is a CLAIM never a verdict — the daemon probes no process and a sidecar can report `process` for one that died a second ago — AND the absence of a kind is not evidence of death, because a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker.
- `ExecutionAttempt` gains `presenceKind?: AttemptPresenceKind` and `presenceAt?: string`, placed immediately after the existing `processStartedAt`/`host` advisory hints and commented in the same spirit. Both optional, so every attempt record written before today stays valid: no migration, no schemaVersion bump, same additive shape as the hints and `Task.planRevision` before them.

`src/state/attemptStore.ts`:
- Module-level `PRESENCE_KINDS` ReadonlySet (the four, as the single source of truth for validation).
- New exported `recordAttemptPresence(state, attemptId, kind)`, placed between `setAttemptPhase` and `reconcileRunningAttempts`. It writes `presenceKind` + `presenceAt` through the store's persist-then-publish ordering (`writeEntity` then `map.set`, over a private copy so a thrown write cannot have altered published state) and touches NOTHING else — phase, lastPhaseAt, startedAt, generation and the identity hints all come through by spread.
- Its comment states the rule in capitals and gives the reason, so the next editor does not fold it into the phase setter: `setAttemptPhase` stamps `lastPhaseAt`, sweeps.ts measures the reconcile window from that field, and a 60s-per-seat ping through the phase setter would make a reconciling attempt immortal and silently disable the sweep.
- Unknown kind → `invalidInput('presenceKind', ...)` (thrown, nothing stored). Missing attempt → `MoeError NOT_FOUND` with codeName `ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND`, matching `setAttemptPhase`'s existing refusal exactly rather than a silent no-op.

Nothing else in the store changed; `setAttemptPhase`, `closeOpenAttempts` and `reconcileRunningAttempts` are byte-identical. Both files edited with the Edit tool per the step-1 attribution override.

implementationPlan.description: TURN THE PING INTO A REATTACHMENT CHANNEL. In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/heartbeat.ts add an optional presence-kind property to the input schema, keeping workerId required and additionalProperties false, and rewrite the handler in this order. First look up the worker record: when it is missing, return the reattach-required response immediately and do not call touchWorker, since there is nothing to refresh and the point is to tell the sidecar to re-register. When the worker exists, refresh it with touchWorker exactly as today, because keeping lastActivityAt fresh during a long silent build is this tool's original job and the rule that a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker depends on it. Then resolve the caller's open attempt: no open attempt means reattach-required; an attempt in the reconciling phase also means reattach-required, and in that case do NOT record presence, because a runner that has not proven it is there must not be able to look present. Otherwise, when and only when a presence kind was supplied, record it through the new store function — so an old-style ping performs no extra write at all, which is what the definition of done means by adding no new disk write per ping beyond the presence field. The reattach-required response must be a returned value, not a thrown error: this tool fires every sixty seconds from a sidecar and a throw would turn a routine restart into an error loop in the wrapper log. Make it clearly distinguishable from an acknowledgement, carry a stable reason naming which of the three conditions fired, include the attempt id and phase when an attempt exists, and point the caller at the reattach tool by name. Error handling for a genuinely unexpected store failure stays as it is today: the tool must not become a source of fleet-wide noise. Do not mark the tool blocking, and do not add runExclusive.

implementationPlan.description: DOCUMENT THE NEW CONTRACT. Extend the existing `moe.heartbeat` section in docs/MCP_SERVER.md rather than adding a second one: add the optional presence-kind parameter with its four values and what each one means, document both response shapes, and list the three conditions that produce reattach-required — no worker record, no open attempt, and an attempt in the reconciling phase. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Recording presence through the existing `setAttemptPhase`, re-asserting the current phase: rejected, and this is the most important decision in the card. That function stamps `lastPhaseAt`, and the reconcile-window sweep from task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c measures its window from that field, so a sixty-second ping would make a reconciling attempt immortal and silently disable that sweep. Presence gets its own writer that never touches the phase timestamp, and a test asserts the stored bytes to keep it that way. (2) Throwing a MoeError for reattach-required: rejected, because this tool fires every sixty seconds from a sidecar and a throw turns a routine daemon restart into an error loop in the wrapper log. It is a returned value carrying a stable reason. (3) Making the presence kind required: rejected outright by a task rail — an un-upgraded wrapper sends nothing and must keep working, so the field is optional and a pingless-of-presence call performs no extra write at all. (4) Recording presence for an attempt in the reconciling phase: rejected, since a runner that has not proven it is there must not be able to look present; that ping gets reattach-required and writes nothing. (5) Calling touchWorker before the worker lookup, as today's code effectively does: reordered so a missing worker returns immediately, because there is nothing to refresh and the response is the whole point. (6) Adding runExclusive: rejected — tool dispatch is already serialized through the global state mutex and this handler must stay cheap.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: No acceptance case names this card, confirmed by grepping the task id against src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, so the card is the contract — unlike the last several Wave 1 cards. heartbeat.ts is 34 lines: workerId required, one touchWorker call, a bare acknowledgement, and a header comment that already explains why touchWorker no-ops on a missing or dead record, which is precisely the defect this card fixes. It deliberately does not wrap itself in runExclusive because MCP dispatch is already serialized. The attempt store already follows a persist-then-publish ordering per mutation and already carries optional advisory hints for process start time and host, with a comment saying plainly that they narrow which process is meant and prove nothing about liveness — the new presence fields belong in exactly that spirit and with the same optionality, so no migration is needed. `listAttempts` and `currentAttempt` give the lookup; `currentAttempt` returns the single non-closed attempt, which is what a sidecar's ping should resolve to. src/tools/heartbeat.test.ts already exists, so no new test file. docs/MCP_SERVER.md already has a heartbeat section to extend rather than duplicate.
planningNotes.risks: The one defect that would pass review and cause real damage is routing the presence write through the phase setter: it looks like reuse, and it would quietly neutralise the reconcile-window sweep planned this session. The test must assert the stored phase timestamp byte-for-byte, not merely that the phase string is unchanged. Second, this tool runs every sixty seconds for every seat, so any extra work is multiplied fleet-wide: no exclusive section, no extra write on an old-style ping, and no throw on the reattach paths. Third, keep touchWorker for a live worker — removing or short-circuiting it makes a long silent build start looking dead, which is the exact rule the epic forbids breaking. Fourth, the reattach-required response names a tool delivered by the sibling restart card; if that has not landed, name it anyway and say so rather than inventing a second surface. Finally, be honest in the handoff: the wrapper does not send the new field yet, so the presence data is inert until the sibling wrapper task lands, and a presence kind is a self-report rather than evidence.
